chordInfo.name: Power Chords
chordInfo.subtitle: Master the driving force behind rock, punk, metal, and grunge with power chords - the raw, aggressive two-note shapes that define electric guitar.

fundamentals.label: Definition
fundamentals.value: Two-note chords containing only a root and perfect 5th

fundamentals.label: Function
fundamentals.value: Neither major nor minor - ambiguous tonality

applications.label: Rock & Metal
applications.value: Driving riffs, palm-muted chugging, heavy rhythm

applications.label: Punk
applications.value: Fast chord changes, raw energy, three-chord songs

applications.label: Grunge
applications.value: Dirty tones, drop tunings, angular riffs

applications.label: Pop-Rock
applications.value: Chorus power, dynamic contrast with clean verses

boxes.title: E5 Power Chord Example
items: Root: E (1st degree)
Perfect 5th: B (5th degree)
Octave: E (optional doubling)
Semitones: E to B = 7 semitones
Result: Neutral, powerful dyad

boxes.title: Why No Third?
items: No major 3rd: Not bright or happy
No minor 3rd: Not dark or sad
Ambiguous quality: Works over anything
Distortion-friendly: Fewer overtone clashes
Versatile: Fits major and minor keys

boxes.title: Moveable Shape Advantage
items: Two shapes: 6th-string and 5th-string root
Same fingering everywhere on the neck
No open strings needed after learning shapes
Easy transposition: slide up or down frets
Full neck coverage with just two forms

voicingGroups.title: Essential Open Power Chords
voicingGroups.tipDescription: These open-position power chords are the easiest to play and appear in countless rock songs. Focus on clean two- or three-string voicings.

voicings.name: E5
voicings.use: Rock anthems, metal riffs, drop D staple

voicingGroups.title: Moveable Power Chord Forms
voicingGroups.tipDescription: Once you learn the 6th-string root and 5th-string root shapes, you can play any power chord anywhere on the neck. These two forms are the foundation of rock rhythm guitar.

voicings.name: 6th-String Root Form
voicings.fingering: Index on root, ring finger two frets up on next string
voicings.use: E5 through Eb5 - covers all notes on the 6th string

voicings.name: 5th-String Root Form
voicings.fingering: Index on root, ring finger two frets up on next string
voicings.use: A5 through Ab5 - covers all notes on the 5th string

items.title: Classic Rock I-IV-V

strumming.description: Driving rock rhythm with palm muting

items.description: The backbone of rock and roll - this three-chord power chord progression drives songs like "Johnny B. Goode" and "Back in Black"

items.title: Punk Progression I-V-vi-IV

strumming.pattern: D D D D D D D D

items.description: Fast downstrokes with distortion create the driving intensity of punk rock - used in countless Ramones, Green Day, and Blink-182 songs

items.title: Metal Riff i-bVI-bVII-i
items.description: The minor-key power chord progression that defines heavy metal - heard in Iron Maiden, Black Sabbath, and Metallica riffs

items.title: Grunge Verse-Chorus i-iv-i-V
items.description: The raw, unpolished power chord movement that defined 90s grunge - characteristic of Nirvana, Pearl Jam, and Soundgarden

techniqueItems: Keep your fretting hand fingers arched to mute unused strings
Practice palm muting for tight, percussive rhythm
Use all downstrokes for punk-style intensity
Slide between chord positions for smooth transitions
applicationItems: The universal language of rock guitar since the 1950s
Works with any level of distortion or gain
Perfect for writing riffs and song ideas quickly
Essential for playing along with almost any rock song

practiceExercises.title: Practice Exercises
practiceExercises.tipDescription: Focus on clean string muting, precise fretting, and rhythmic accuracy. Power chords sound sloppy if extra strings ring out.

exercises.title: Exercise 1: Chromatic Power Chord Walk
exercises.content: Pattern: F5 - F#5 - G5 - Ab5 - A5 (1st fret to 5th fret, 6th-string root)
exercises.detail: Play each chord for four beats, moving up one fret at a time on the 6th string root form. Then descend back down.
exercises.tip: Keep your index and ring fingers locked in the same shape - only your arm position should change as you slide up the neck

exercises.title: Exercise 2: String-Switching Drill
exercises.content: Pattern: E5 - A5 - D5 - A5 - E5 (alternating 6th and 5th string roots)
exercises.detail: Practice switching between 6th-string root chords and 5th-string root chords while maintaining a steady eighth-note rhythm.
exercises.tip: Mute unused strings with the underside of your index finger to prevent unwanted noise when switching string sets

exercises.title: Exercise 3: Palm-Muted Riff Building
exercises.content: Pattern: E5 (muted) - E5 (open) - G5 - A5 - E5 with palm muting
exercises.detail: Alternate between palm-muted and open power chords to create dynamics. Rest the edge of your picking hand on the bridge.
exercises.tip: Adjust palm mute pressure for different levels of tightness - light pressure for a chunky sound, firm pressure for a muted percussive tick

concepts.title: Drop Tunings & Extended Voicings
items: Drop D: Tune 6th string to D for one-finger power chords
Drop C / Drop B: Heavier tunings for modern metal tones
Octave doubling: Add the octave with your pinky for a fuller sound
Root-5th-octave-5th: Four-string voicing for massive walls of sound
Inverted power chords: Put the 5th in the bass for a different character

concepts.title: Rhythmic Techniques & Textures
items: Palm muting: Control sustain and create chugging rhythms
Gallop picking: Down-down-up pattern for driving metal riffs
Syncopation: Accent off-beats for funk-rock and groove metal feels
Staccato hits: Short, punchy chords with quick muting for tight passages
Harmonics layering: Natural harmonics over power chord shapes for shimmering effects

journeySection.title: Continue Your Chord Journey
journeySection.description: Power chords are the gateway to rock guitar. Expand your harmonic vocabulary by exploring major and minor triads, then add color with seventh chords.

links.title: Major Chords
links.description: Add the major 3rd to hear the bright, full sound that power chords leave out.

links.title: Minor Chords
links.description: Discover the dark, emotional side by adding a minor 3rd to your root and 5th.

links.title: Seventh Chords
links.description: Extend your power chords with 7ths for blues, jazz, and sophisticated rock tones.
